_comment: Where live 2026 results come from, per state, and — just as important —
which states we probed and could NOT get. This is a data file rather than
code because the list changes on election night as states publish, and
because a reader of the dashboard deserves to know that an empty state
means 'we cannot read their feed', not 'nobody voted'.
THERE IS NO FREE NATIONAL LIVE-RESULTS FEED. AP's Elections API is the
industry standard and is paid. Everything here is a per-state adapter,
because every state publishes differently, and most publish in a shape
built for a browser rather than for a program.
working              - parsed successfully, verified on last_verified
awaiting_publication - endpoint is real, the 2026 file is not there yet
blocked              - reachable but refuses automated clients
spa_only             - a JavaScript app with no static feed we could find

NC.format: zip containing tab-delimited txt, precinct level
notes: 141,467 precinct rows. Contest Type C = county, S = state/federal.
Carries votes broken out by mode, which most states do not.
Publishes NO explicit precincts-reporting count. We therefore record
precincts_with_votes and precincts_total and leave precincts_reporting
null: a precinct can legitimately report zero for one contest, so
counting non-zero precincts would overstate how complete a count is.
At 13:20 ET on election day the file is the pre-published ballot
template, every vote zero, Last-Modified 2026-10-05. That is the
correct answer before polls close, not a parse failure.
The directory is real and returns 200, and Virginia documents a JSON
results file on its reporting site. Neither carries 2026 general data
yet — the listing is empty of 2026 files as of 2026-11-03 13:20 ET.
Clarity is the vendor behind many states and counties, so solving it
once would unlock several. It sits behind an AWS WAF challenge:
HTTP 202, x-amzn-waf-action: challenge, zero-length body to any
plain HTTP client. It needs a real browser, which is out of scope
for this ingest and deliberately not worked around.
Single-page app with a catch-all route: every path returns the same
~15KB HTML with HTTP 200, including deliberately invented ones. Any
probe that looks like a working endpoint here is a false positive,
which is why each candidate path was tested against a nonsense
control before being believed.
403 to automated clients, on both real and control paths.
403 to automated clients.
Index page is still templated — it literally contains the unreplaced
placeholder {*GENERAL_ELECTION_CODE*}. Only a precinct reference
spreadsheet is posted.
The canonical national early-vote tracker. The page renders the CSV
client-side with PapaParse, so the CSV itself is the stable interface.
Each row carries its OWN last_update and the underlying state source,
which is what we store — UF aggregates states that report on different
days, so a single national 'as of' would be a fiction.
ZERO DOES NOT MEAN ZERO. Where a state does not report a breakdown, UF
writes 0 rather than leaving it blank. Alaska reports 99,424 votes cast
and 0 Democrats, 0 Republicans — because Alaska does not report party
registration, not because no Democrat voted. Any breakdown whose parts
are all zero while the total is positive is stored as null.
